cognate: Lith. prašyti = ORu просити (*proḱ-éye-, o-grade iterative of *preḱ- 'ask'); Lith. maldyti (beside melsti) = ORu молити (*moldʰ-éye-, o-grade iterative of *meldʰ- 'pray'). Both members of the pair are cognate and, in the maldyti variant, morphologically identical (same o-grade -eye- formation).
drift_or_renewal: none (Lith. alternates the primary verb melsti with maldyti; ORu adds reflexive сѧ to молити)
shared_syntax: coordinated (Lith. mostly asyndetic) synonym binomial of two verbs of entreaty, same order 'ask, pray' in Lith.; ORu 'pray and ask (for peace)', same pair inverted
context: supplication of a person in power: in the dainos the suitor/bride entreats the father or mother (tėvą prašyti, maldyti); in the Suzdal chronicle the besieged prince entreats the besieger for peace. The dainos repeat the pair as a fixed refrain-like formula (some 20 hits); OCS also couples the two verbs (Gospel calque contexts).

cognate: *tekʷ- 'run' specialised to 'flow (of water)' in Lith. tekėti, ORu течи, Av. tac-, with cognate water nouns: *h₂ep- (Lith. upė, Av. āp-) and *srow- 'stream' (Lith. srovė, ORu струя)
drift_or_renewal: none; the shared semantic step is 'run' > 'flow' of water (Vedic tak- shows no such use)
shared_syntax: water noun as subject of intransitive *tekʷ- (Lith. upės teka / Av. āpō taciṇti); Lith. 'teka srovės upelis' ~ Igor 'течетъ ... струями' with *srow- noun beside the verb
context: rivers/waters running in descriptive or ritual passages (Av. Vīdēvdād: waters flow from the sea; Lith. dainos and Igor: the river runs past the place). Avestan āpō taciṇti is a recurrent formula (5 of 28 Av. *tekʷ- units), Lith. upė teka recurrent (16 hits).
phrase: *h₂ápes tékʷonti 'the waters run' (Av., Lith.); *tekʷ- + *srow- 'run with streams' (Lith., ORu)

cognate: Lith. joti = SCr. jezditi (*yeh₂- 'ride, go'); Lith. giria 'forest' = SCr. gora 'forested mountain' (*gʷorH-); Lith. žalias = SCr. zelen (*ǵʰel- 'green')
drift_or_renewal: gora has kept 'mountain' beside 'forest'; the epithet is stable
shared_syntax: verb of riding + (prefix/preposition) + acc. of noun 'forest' with epithet 'green': prijojo žalią girę ~ језди кроз гору зелену
context: the young man/hero riding on horseback through the green forest in ballad narrative; žalia giria and gora zelena are each stock formulas (8 and 117 hits).
phrase: *ǵʰel- + *gʷorH- 'green forest' as object of riding (*yeh₂-), Balto-Slavic folk-poetic formula

cognate: Lith. vesti = ORu вести (*wedʰ- 'lead (home) a bride', cf. Ved. vadhū́-, Av. vād-, OIr. fedid, W. dyweddi); Lith. dukra/duktė = ORu дъщи (*dʰugh₂tḗr)
drift_or_renewal: none; Lith. active of the bridegroom, ORu passive of the bride given in marriage
shared_syntax: *wedʰ- with 'daughter (of the father/of X)' as patient: tėvo dukrelę vedęs ~ ведена дщи Святополча за Болеслава
context: marriage: Lith. wedding song asks the groom whether he has married the father's daughter; the Laurentian chronicle's recurring formula for dynastic marriage (three hits). Inherited is the marriage sense of *wedʰ- (recalled); the daughter+genitive of the father may be natural, so low.

cognate: *tekʷ- 'run' of the course of sun and moon (Lith. tekėti 'rise', SCr. teći, Ru. течь in byliny); sun *sóh₂wl̥ and moon *mḗh₁n̥s cognate
drift_or_renewal: Lith. tekėti narrowed to 'rise'; SCr. 'dokle teče sunca' = 'as far as the sun runs' (extent)
shared_syntax: sun and moon paired with *tekʷ- in one line (Lith. imperative to the moon; SCr. sun and moon in gen. with teče)
context: heavenly bodies' course: Lith. lyric bidding sun set and moon rise; SCr. epic 'as far as sun and moon run' = the whole world. Contexts differ; shared is the idiom *tekʷ- of the sun's/moon's course, Balto-Slavic only, late traditions.

search_lead.cognate: *médʰu 'mead' (Lith. midus, Gk μέθυ, OE medu, Ved. mádhu) with 'sweet': *swéh₂du- in Gk ἡδύ, OE swēte, Ved. svādú-; Lith. renews the adjective with saldus; drink verb Lith. gerti renews *peh₃- (Ved. piba)
search_lead.argument: Lith. 'gersim ... saldų midų' / 'saldaus midaus atsigėręs' continues the epithet+noun 'sweet mead' found in Homer (formulaic μέθυ ἡδύ), OE and Vedic; Lith. has the noun cognate but the adjective renewed. The slab partners (AV salila) are mapping hits, not parallels. Lith. midus may be influenced by Slavic/German; 'sweet' of mead is natural, so moderate value.

near_miss.why_not: Lith. = gossiping matchmaker; Skt. = epithet of demons/monsters (also MBh, Rām). 'long tongue' for a gossip is a widespread image; contexts not congruent.
